title: Systematic investigation of a possible occupational cause of lung cancer in two patient collectives at Universitätsklinikum Erlangen
summary:
Various non-occupational but also occupational factors can be pathogenetically relevant in the development of lung cancer, which can also occur simultaneously or interact. Occupational activities that are associated with an increased risk of developing lung cancer are diverse and can be associated with a wide variety of occupational groups. 

In a cooperation project between the Institute and Outpatient Clinic of Occupational, Social-, and Environmental Medicine (IPASUM) of Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, and the Department of Medicine 1 at Universitätsklinikum Erlangen, we aim to determine how many patients with a diagnosis of lung cancer from two patient collectives at Universitätsklinikum Erlangen must be suspected of having an occupational disease. A detailed occupational history is taken from the patients. The results of the medical history are examined at IPASUM by doctors with experience in occupational medicine. If there is a well-founded suspicion of the existence of an occupational disease, this suspicion is reported to the responsible body (usually the employer's accident insurance) and the patient is informed of this report. In addition to the occupational history, the available clinical and molecular pathological data are recorded (e.g. tumor classification, clinical course) in order to be able to show possible correlations between these parameters and the anamnestic information (e.g. exposure to certain noxious substances at the workplace).
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung

interventions.name: Patients with lung cancer whose cases will be discussed between July 2026 and June 2028 as part of the tumor board at Universitätsklinikum Erlangen (estimated at approx. 400 people).

Patients with a diagnosis of lung cancer who are treated at Department of Medicine 1,  Universitästklinikum Erlangen, in the period from March to April 2025 (estimated 150 people). An overlap between collectives 1 and 2 is possible and will be taken into account in the analysis.
